translationRepairs: Chen Tanlang, Prince Min of Nankang, was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, the Founder's maternal uncle.
Chen Tanlang, Prince Min of Nankang, was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, the Founder's younger brother by the same mother.
高祖母弟 means Gaozu’s uterine younger brother (母弟), not maternal uncle; the proposed phrasing restores that kinship.
Prince Min of Nankang Chen Tanlang was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, younger brother of the Founder's mother.
Prince Min of Nankang Chen Tanlang was the son of Prince Zhongzhuang Xiuxian, the Founder's younger brother by the same mother.
高祖母弟 parses as Gaozu’s 母弟 (uterine younger brother), not ‘younger brother of the Founder’s mother’; the replacement matches that reading.
In Tiankang year two, when peace was made with Qi, the court first learned he was dead.
In Tianjia year two, when peace was made with Qi, the court first learned he was dead.
天嘉 romanizes as Tianjia; Tiankang would be 天康, a different Chen era name.
In the second year of Tiankang, when Qi made peace, they first learned of it.
In the second year of Tianjia, when Qi made peace, they first learned of it.
天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiankang; only the era romanization needs correction.

In Tiankang year one an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang is held in Qi and cannot return; the ancestral temple is being restored and needs a master—let his eldest son Fangtai be heir of Nankang and succeed the title."

In Tianjia year one an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang is held in Qi and cannot return; the ancestral temple is being restored and needs a master—let his eldest son Fangtai be heir of Nankang and succeed the title."
天嘉元年 is the first year of Tianjia; Tiankang misreads 嘉 as 康.

In the first year of Tiankang, an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang, cut off in the Qi court, his return uncertain; the state temple is being restored and sacrifices need a master—his eldest son Fangtai may be made Heir of Nankang and succeed the Prince of Nankang."

In the first year of Tianjia, an edict said: "Prince of Nankang Chen Tanlang, cut off in the Qi court, his return uncertain; the state temple is being restored and sacrifices need a master—his eldest son Fangtai may be made Heir of Nankang and succeed the Prince of Nankang."
Literal field has the same 天嘉→Tianjia error; the proposed romanization is correct.
During Tiankang he was enfeoffed as marquis of Linru.
During Tianjia he was enfeoffed as marquis of Linru.
天嘉中 is during the Tianjia era, not Tiankang.
In the Tiankang era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linru county.
In the Tianjia era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linru county.
Same 天嘉→Tianjia correction as the idiomatic field; the rest of the literal already matches the Chinese.
When Gui and the rest were put to death, the northerners also killed Tanlang at Jinyang; he was twenty-eight. (The text supplies the missing word "year".)
When Gui and the rest were put to death, the northerners also killed Tanlang at Jinyang; he was twenty-eight.
時年二十八 supports ‘he was twenty-eight’; the parenthetical about supplying ‘year’ is translator commentary, not Chinese text.
